title: The Princess and the Pea
author: Hans Christian Andersen
source: Public domain. Retold from Hans Christian Andersen.

characters.name: The Princess
characters.voiceHint: a polite but very tired voice

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Once upon a time there was a prince who wished to marry a princess — but she had to be a real princess, through and through. He traveled the whole world over looking for one.

segments.speaker: prince
segments.text: "Princesses are everywhere. But how can I ever be sure one is a REAL princess?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At last he came home again, feeling very sad indeed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one evening, a terrible storm blew in. Thunder boomed, lightning flashed, and the rain came down in buckets. In the middle of it all, there came a knocking at the palace gate. The old king himself went to open it.

segments.speaker: king
segments.text: "Well, bless my crown! Who would be out on a night like this?"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There at the gate stood a girl, dripping from head to toe. Water ran from her hair and her clothes, into the toes of her shoes and out again at the heels.

segments.speaker: princess
segments.text: "Good evening. I am terribly sorry to trouble you — but I am a real princess, and I have lost my way in the storm."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A princess? Looking like THAT? The old queen said nothing, but she had her own way of finding out the truth.

segments.speaker: queen
segments.text: "A real princess, is she? We shall soon see about that. I shall put one tiny pea on the bedstead — and pile twenty mattresses on top of it, and twenty feather beds on top of the mattresses. Only a REAL princess could feel a pea through all of that!"

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: whispered the old queen to herself. And that is exactly what she did.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The princess climbed a tall ladder to the very top of the twenty mattresses and twenty feather beds, said her thank-yous and good-nights, and settled in to sleep. In the morning, the whole family gathered at breakfast.

segments.speaker: king
segments.text: "Well, my dear! And how did you sleep?"

segments.speaker: princess
segments.text: "Oh, terribly, I am sorry to say! I hardly closed my eyes all night. There was something hard in that bed — I am black and blue all over! I simply cannot imagine what it was."

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The queen clapped her hands. She had felt the pea through twenty mattresses and twenty feather beds — nobody but a real princess could be so tender.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: cried the prince joyfully. And so the prince and the princess were married, and they lived long and happily together.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As for the pea? It was put in a museum, where it may be seen to this very day — if nobody has taken it. And that, you may be sure, is a true story.
